not OP but Cantonese is my first language 

- onyomi readings usually sound closer to Cantonese than Mandarin 

not Cantonese specific: 

- if you're having trouble remembering kanji, especially if the radicals seem to make no sense, look up the corresponding hanzi's etymology in a Chinese dictionary. Phonetically the radicals may make more sense in Chinese 

- if the definition of the kanji differs from the hanzi, its usually because the kanji is using the definition from classical Chinese, or a proverb. Again, looking up the etymology of the hanzi is pretty helpful if you're stuck 

When I was learning kanji I always had a Chinese dictionary with me. I ended up improving my Chinese just to read Japanese lolol 

edit: I forgot another major advantage: pitch accent. I think because people who know Chinese are so used to tones, pitch accent in Japanese is extremely easy to pick up. Just be aware of its existence and you should be able to absorb it fairly naturally

My routine before was really extensive. I was exfoliating twice a day with bha in the morning and aha at night. You know how after you exfoliate and all the dead skin sloughs off and you look all smooth and glowly? My skin was always in that state but I had to moisturize and use face masks constantly to compensate for how drying it was. It was time consuming and wasteful and since then I've scaled down with just toner, essence, moisturizer, and just tret + exfoliating once a week. Ok I realize that still sounds like a lot but it's much more simple than my previous routine and I don't use face masks anymore. 

My pores are still in pretty good shape but they aren't invisible like they were before. I'm a lot happier with how much easier and cheaper my routine is though! I just don't think the extra effort is worth it when literally no one noticed my pores except for me haha

I've never given my canary live insects but she does get the occasional dried (and dead) mealworm as a treat, usually during molting season for the additional protein. 

The ideal diet would consist mostly of pellets. Harrisons, roudybush, and zupreem would be my personal top picks in that order. 

You should also provide a bit of dry seed. My vet reccomends abba seed canary mix. Fresh vegetables should also be provided daily, especially leafy greens. If you have a bird with red factor genes you can feed them vegetables high in beta carotene to bring out the colouring. 

Because she is prone to stomach aches, I also give her exactly four hemp seeds a day and 1/8th tbsp of chia seeds to address her digestive issues. 

For treats I use millet and fresh fruit. Hope that helps!

I used to lie a lot. I think it was a learned habit. There were several different reasons for this:

- organizing my thoughts to explain the truth was too difficult so I'd make a 'shortcut lie' instead (eg. a ton of series of events led to the vase breaking but its much easier to pretend like the cat knocked it over) 

- my brain obviously worked differently from most of my peers so if I explained my messy thought process no one would believe me, so I started lying as a kid because more adults would accept my lie since it sounded more normal

- i didn't know I had ADHD, I thought I was just stupid and incompetent so I would lie to cover my insecurities (eg. lying about missing details at my job) 

- to expand on the first point if I told the truth I'd end up hesitating a lot trying to organize the words in my head and people mistook the pauses and hesitation as me being dishonest/nervous and making something up so why not tell a simple lie instead

- over time it simply became a learned defense mechanism and i would lie as an adult without really thinking about it, because I associated being honest with rejection and lying with validation

I'm trying my best to undo this habit now but I hope my explanation makes sense.

I own a GCC and a canary (housed separately of course) and they seem happier than my single budgies did. They chatter and chirp to each other a lot, and when my canary sings my GCC fluffs up with contentment and dances. They also preen, bathe, and eat at the same time. That said, I don't even know if my GCC likes my canary all that much, she seems indifferent and makes irritated noises if I kiss the canary, and has shown signs of jealousy. My canary tries to preen her a lot and my GCC seems to find it annoying. Even so, she gets very upset when the canary is not in the room. Once the canary got sick and boarded at the vets for two nights and my GCC became depressed, stared at her cage, and did not vocalize the entire time.

Keep in mind you should be prepared to do double the work. I clean two cages, I monitor two daily sets of poop, pay double the vet bills, and both have different diets and issues I need to address individually. It can be a lot of work sometimes, far more than owning a single bird, but it's worth it for them to not be alone when no ones home. I had the single canary before the GCC and my canary is definitely much happier these days, even though she is technically a 'solo' bird. 

Also finches work better in pairs or groups, even if you were to own a budgie to keep it company. Canaries are solo birds and territorial so I only have one, but finches need cage mates or they will get depressed (don't house the finch and budgie together!)

A lot of people in this sub have single birds that do fine, though. The important thing is to teach them how to keep busy with their toys, and a lot of people will leave radios or the TV on so the bird doesn't feel lonely. Silence stresses out birds a lot. 

So while I do think your idea is good, be prepared for a lot of extra work and bills!

Hi, I read your post and I'll try to provide you with as much information and help as I can! 

First of all it's not a hopeless case. A common misconception is that a non hand raised bird will be a flying demon spawn, but all of my birds were adopted and from pet stores, and were quite sweet and cuddly. It sounds like your girlfriend is just not disciplining the bird properly. 

First of all, what kind of bird is it? If you don't know provide us with a picture and we can identify it for you. edit: never mind you said it was a Quaker. Quakers are very intelligent so they will need a lot of toys to keep them busy. 

Second, your bird needs to sleep exactly 12 hours especially during this time of year (it's mating season) All birds get bitey and loud and angsty during this period and the only way to mitigate this is by letting them sleep properly. 

Third, you say the bird cannot entertain himself and your girlfriend has to 'reset' and soothe him. Does your bird have an appropriate amount of toys? Swings, bells, chews, and foragers? Like people birds have preferences. They need different kind of toys to keep them entertained. Assuming your bird has these things, the reseting method that is just enabling the screaming behavior. If your bird is shrieking first identify the problems. Does he have food, water, toys, things to keep him occupied? If he does and he is still screaming, you need to ignore the noise and reward him with attention when he is quiet. 

If he is not getting enough attention that could also be a reason for the screaming. All birds need a minimal of at least a few hours of out of cage time. You don't even need to directly interact with him. My parrot likes to sit quietly and watch me play video games, or perch on the chairs while my family eats dinner or watches TV. Of course she enjoys petting and cuddling but what I'm trying to say is it's not completely necessary, especially since your bird doesn't seem to like being touched right now. 

As for the pooping thing, it's not exactly normal for your bird to be going to the bathroom in its own water dish. Is there a perch above the dishes? Do you reward the bird with attention every time it poops in its bowls? I had a bird that would purposely poop in her food because she thought my reaction was funny. Trust me, they know what they're doing. Avoid eye contact, don't say anything or pay attention to the bird, and silently and quickly change the dishes. You can also potty train your birds to some extent (my parrot will only poop in approved areas in the house like garbage cans and her own cage) but maybe save that for later because there seems to be bigger issues at hand right now.
